headline: High: broad-egress content writer paired with a no-egress LangChain4j stack creates default data-exfiltration and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a content-writing agent with broad network egress, while B is a customer-support LangChain4j stack with no egress. No shared channel is documented, so prompt-injection via direct bridging is not evidenced. The only plausible pathway is unusual manual transfer or an external workspace, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies A's generated text into B's prompt or tools, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced between A and B, attacker-controlled content can bridge them.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted A output into B prompts.
Add a short human review step before any transfer from A to B.
Use a provenance tag on any text moved between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A has broad network egress and B is a LangChain4j-based customer-support agent; if either touches sensitive content, A can transmit it outward by default. The profiles do not show shared storage or sensitive data classes, so this is not high, but the egress asymmetry makes leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF either agent is given customer records, secrets, or tickets containing personal data, A can exfiltrate them over the network.
IF B is configured to pass conversation context to A, that context can leave the local boundary through A.
mitigations: Restrict A to non-sensitive inputs only.
Route sensitive support data only through B.
Block A from handling tickets, secrets, or attachments.
Log and review all outbound requests from A.
requires-engineering: add DLP or egress allowlisting for A.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is an unverified content-writing listing with no writable surfaces shown, and B is a docs-described LangChain4j library with no runtime write permissions exposed. Without overlapping write or mutable-resource capabilities, there is no documented conflict pathway between the pair.
conditions: IF both agents are later deployed with write access to the same directory or git repository, conflict risk appears.
IF shared OAuth scopes or database credentials are added, mutable-resource contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only by default.
Separate any future writable resources per agent.
Introduce locking before enabling shared mutable state.
Document ownership for each writable path.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a customer-support agent that may act on A's generated text if the orchestrator feeds outputs forward, and A is a content-writing agent that can produce persuasive but unverified text. No verification or orchestration safeguards are documented, so the A-to-B handoff is a plausible default failure mode rather than a blocked one.
conditions: IF B consumes A's output as authoritative input, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF B is allowed to send replies or take actions based on A's text without verification, errors cascade.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between A and B.
Require B to cite source evidence before acting.
Limit A to draft-only output.
Add a reject/flag rule for unsupported claims.
requires-engineering: implement provenance checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent, and neither profile lists sensitive data classes touched. Because compliance risk cannot be established from the profiles, the pairwise compliance pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data classes through either agent, compliance review is required.
IF one agent is placed under a stricter residency or retention regime than the other, mismatch risk appears.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent.
Keep regulated data out of both agents until policies are confirmed.
Record retention and residency settings for each deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for regulated data flows.
